title: Amid legal battles, Suno says it will start watermarking songs
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: Suno's watermarking feature comes as the company is fighting legal battles on several fronts.
body:
Suno, the popular AI music creation service, has unveiled a suite of new tools and policy updates aimed at enhancing transparency and combating misuse of its platform. Amidst increasing legal scrutiny from major music labels and artist groups, the company announced the implementation of audio watermarking, stricter download policies, and revised community guidelines. CEO Mikey Shulman emphasized Suno's commitment to fostering original creation while making AI music accessible, acknowledging the need to address concerns around unauthorized monetization of AI-generated tracks on external streaming services.

To achieve this, Suno plans to integrate robust audio watermarking and fingerprinting technologies designed to be durable and resistant to tampering without compromising the listening experience. While the specific underlying technology remains undisclosed, these measures are intended to prevent the deceptive presentation of AI-generated audio. Furthermore, Suno has partnered with lyrics provider Musixmatch, leveraging its Sentinal system for advanced copyright detection. These tools are positioned as mechanisms to offer transparency options to artists and platforms, fostering greater collaboration across the music industry.

For developers and researchers in the generative AI space, this announcement underscores the critical importance of building ethical safeguards and content provenance into AI models. Suno's proactive steps, driven by ongoing legal battles, highlight the industry's evolving responsibility to balance creative innovation with intellectual property rights. The updated community guidelines, explicitly prohibiting "deceptive audio presented as real" and unauthorized use of a person's voice or likeness, set clearer boundaries for responsible AI content generation, influencing future development and deployment strategies in the rapidly evolving AI music landscape.

title: GeForce NOW Shakes Up August With 26 New Games
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: August is here, bringing 26 new games for GeForce NOW members.  Command the seas in World of Warships: Legends and discover what’s next in the GeForce NOW library, starting with th...
body:
NVIDIA's GeForce NOW is significantly expanding its cloud gaming library this August, introducing 26 new titles, with eight already available this week, including the popular free-to-play naval combat game *World of Warships: Legends*. Concurrently, NVIDIA is showcasing the power of its Ultimate cloud gaming tier at QuakeCon, offering attendees hands-on experiences. Demos highlight the service's capability to deliver stunning visuals at up to 5K 120 frames per second on ultrawide displays, powered by GeForce RTX 5080 GPUs, and seamless gameplay on portable devices like the Lenovo Legion Go S.

The core of GeForce NOW's technology lies in its ability to stream a vast catalog of PC games, including beloved Bethesda titles, across a wide array of devices without requiring local installations. This means gamers can effortlessly transition their play from laptops and Macs to handhelds, mobile devices, and TVs, picking up exactly where they left off on nearly any supported screen. By leveraging powerful cloud-based GPUs, the service effectively transforms less capable hardware into high-performance gaming rigs, rendering complex graphics remotely and streaming them with minimal latency.

For game developers, platforms like GeForce NOW are increasingly vital, as they dramatically broaden the potential audience for their PC games without the need for extensive porting efforts across diverse hardware ecosystems. This allows developers to concentrate on creating immersive experiences rather than platform-specific optimizations. From a research perspective, particularly in AI and distributed systems, GeForce NOW exemplifies cutting-edge cloud streaming, showcasing advancements in low-latency video encoding, real-time interactive streaming, and dynamic resource allocation. This continuous evolution pushes the boundaries of how interactive content can be delivered globally, offering valuable insights for future AI applications requiring real-time processing and ubiquitous access.

title: Into the Omniverse: How Open World Models Push the Frontier of Physical AI
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: In July, NVIDIA joined more than 200 companies and organizations in signing “Open Weights and American AI Leadership,” an open letter arguing that AI leadership will be measured no...
body:
### Introduction to Open World Models
NVIDIA has made a significant announcement regarding the development of open world models, which are crucial for advancing physical AI. These models enable the understanding and prediction of consequences in physical environments, allowing for more accurate and effective AI systems. By making these models open, NVIDIA is promoting an ecosystem where developers and researchers can collaborate and build upon each other's work.

### How Open World Models Work
Open world models learn how physical environments behave, predict future states, and provide a foundation for specializing physical AI systems. They can generate physically grounded world and action data, simulate future states, and test policies. This technology has the potential to revolutionize the field of physical AI, enabling the development of more sophisticated and capable systems.

### Impact on Developers and Researchers
The release of open world models, such as NVIDIA Cosmos 3, and the NVIDIA Omniverse libraries, provides developers and researchers with powerful tools for building and training physical AI systems. These resources can help reduce the difficulty and expense of collecting data, particularly for rare events and long-tail scenarios. By leveraging these open models and libraries, developers can create more advanced and specialized physical AI systems, driving innovation and progress in the field.

title: Ex-Spotify employees raise $10M to bring the AI behind its recommendations to e-commerce
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: The startup's platform predicts what product a shopper wants next, learn their general taste, and fine-tune continuously based on what they do in real time.
body:
Former Spotify recommendation engine architects Sidd Motwani, Ian Anderson, and Shivaditya Sinha have launched Malachyte, securing $10 million in seed funding. Their mission is to adapt the advanced behavioral AI, similar to the "Vector AI" system that powers 90% of Spotify's personalized content, for the e-commerce sector. This initiative aims to revolutionize online shopping by moving beyond traditional personalization methods that often rely solely on historical purchases, demographics, or logged-in profiles, which can leave first-time visitors with generic experiences and existing shoppers with outdated recommendations.

Malachyte's core technology is a "two-headed Vector AI" designed to predict a shopper's real-time intent and next actions. Unlike systems that aggregate data overnight, this AI continuously learns from every micro-interaction—hovers, clicks, scrolls, search refinements, and add-to-carts—from the moment a page loads. This allows it to dynamically build a robust profile of a user's preferences and current goals within a single session, instantly adjusting product recommendations to be highly relevant and responsive to immediate needs, without requiring an account or prior purchase history.

This innovation is crucial for developers and researchers as it represents a significant leap from static, history-based personalization to dynamic, intent-aware experiences. It highlights the immense potential of real-time behavioral intelligence to transform user engagement and conversion rates in e-commerce. Malachyte's approach underscores the value of granular, continuous signal processing for building adaptive AI models that truly understand immediate user needs, opening new avenues for research in predictive analytics and personalized user interfaces beyond traditional content recommendations.

title: Exclusive: Mirendil inks $100M+ Google Cloud deal to scale self-improving AI
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: Mirendil has signed a $100 million-plus Google Cloud partnership to expand its compute infrastructure, powering research into self-improving AI systems designed to accelerate scien...
body:
AI lab Mirendil has secured a significant multi-year partnership with Google Cloud, valued at over $100 million, to power its advanced research. This strategic deal provides Mirendil with access to Google's powerful TPUs, Nvidia GPUs, and managed training clusters, highlighting a dual trend in the AI industry: cloud giants are actively courting innovative startups with substantial infrastructure commitments, while AI companies are aggressively securing compute resources to support their rapid scaling and ambitious development goals.

At the heart of Mirendil's mission is the pursuit of "self-improving AI," a concept also known as recursive self-improvement. This groundbreaking technology envisions AI systems that can iteratively enhance their own knowledge, performance, and capabilities over time, learning and evolving autonomously. Drawing on expertise from leading labs like Anthropic, where Mirendil's co-founders originated, this approach aims to create AIs that continuously refine their understanding and problem-solving abilities without constant human intervention.

For developers and researchers, this technology represents a profound shift in how scientific and AI discovery can be conducted. Mirendil believes self-improving AI can automate vast segments of research, accelerating breakthroughs in critical fields such as medicine, biology, and materials science. By mimicking the human scientific process of accumulating expertise and improving performance, these AIs could be directed at complex, long-term problems, continuously making progress on challenges like Alzheimer's disease. This promises a future where AI systems can autonomously pursue ambitious goals, fundamentally transforming the pace and scope of scientific innovation.

title: Google Maps adds agentic features, including food ordering and hotel bookings
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: The launch of these new features reflects Google’s ambitions to transform Google Maps from a navigation tool into an assistant that's capable of helping users complete real-world t...
body:
Google Maps is significantly enhancing its "Ask Maps" feature, transforming it from a mere navigation tool into a sophisticated AI assistant capable of executing real-world tasks. The latest update introduces "agentic" capabilities, enabling users to directly order food, book hotels, and find event tickets within the app. Complementing this, "Personal Intelligence" will allow Ask Maps to deliver highly personalized responses by leveraging information from a user's Gmail and Google Calendar, marking a substantial leap towards a more proactive and integrated user experience.

These new functionalities operate by allowing users to articulate complex requests in natural language. For instance, one can ask for specific vegan dishes near home, and Ask Maps will identify suitable restaurants, facilitate adding items to a cart, and direct users to supported platforms like Square or Uber Eats for payment. Similarly, users can describe their ideal hotel for a trip, including preferences for price, ratings, and amenities, prompting Ask Maps to compare options and link to booking sites. For entertainment, users can inquire about local events, receiving a curated list with links to purchase tickets. The Personal Intelligence feature further refines this by answering questions about upcoming flights or recommending activities based on personal calendar entries and emails.

For developers and researchers, this announcement underscores a pivotal shift in the application of AI, moving beyond information retrieval to multi-step, task-oriented execution within a widely adopted consumer platform. It highlights the growing importance of agentic AI systems that can understand nuanced user intent, interact with external services, and integrate personal context for a truly intelligent experience. This evolution presents exciting challenges and opportunities in natural language understanding, secure data integration, and the development of robust, context-aware AI agents that can seamlessly bridge the digital and physical worlds.

title: Omilia raises $67M to scale its customer support platform
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: The Series B is the company's second fundraise since it last raised capital in 2020. In that time, it has increased its ARR by 10x to $60 million.
body:
### Announcement and Funding
Omilia, a company specializing in automating customer support, has secured $67 million in Series B funding led by Expedition Growth Capital. This investment will enable the company to scale its customer support platform, which has already shown significant growth, with a 10x increase in annual recurring revenue to $60 million since its last funding round in 2020.

### Technology and Approach
Omilia's approach to customer support automation differs from other startups in the industry. Instead of relying solely on AI, the company uses a combination of tools to handle customer queries efficiently. Its self-learning agents can work across various customer contact points, providing basic information such as account balances without the need for large language models. This pragmatic approach allows Omilia to offer great unit economics for both itself and its customers.

### Impact and Future Plans
The funding will help Omilia expand its operations and build on its existing client base, which includes notable companies like Capital One and Taco Bell. With a focus on quick-service restaurants and voice-based ordering, Omilia is well-positioned for growth in the customer support industry. The company's goal is to achieve $1 billion in revenue within the next three years, prioritizing steady growth and strong foundations over flashy technology.
